wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"(1)\n Nothing in subsection (a) shall limit or otherwise affect the availability of funds for drug testing by—\n“(A)\n the Department of Transportation;\n“(B)\n Department of Energy, for employees specifically involved in the handling of nuclear weapons or nuclear materials;\n“(C)\n any agency with an agency-wide drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986; or\n“(D)\n any component of an agency if such component had a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986.\n“(2)\n The Departments of Transportation and Energy and any agency or component thereof with a drug-testing program in existence as of September 15, 1986—\n“(A)\n shall be brought into full compliance with Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below] no later than the end of the 6-month period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act [July 11, 1987]; and\n“(B)\n shall take such actions as may be necessary to ensure that their respective drug-testing programs or plans are brought into full compliance with the mandatory guidelines published under subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii) no later than 90 days after such mandatory guidelines take effect, except that any judicial challenge that affects such guidelines should not affect drug-testing programs or plans subject to this paragraph.\n“(c)\n In the case of an agency (or component thereof) other than an agency as defined by subsection (a)(2) or an agency (or component thereof) covered by subsection (b), none of the funds appropriated or made available by this Act, or any other Act, with respect to any fiscal year, shall be available to administer or implement any drug testing pursuant to Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], or any subsequent order, unless and until—\n“(1)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services provides written certification with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with clauses (i) and (iii) of subsection (a)(1)(A);\n“(2)\n the Secretary of Health and Human Services has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(B); and\n“(3)\n the Director of the Office of Management and Budget has submitted a written, detailed analysis with respect to that agency (or component) in accordance with subsection (a)(1)(C).\n“(d)\n Any Federal employee who is the subject of a drug test under any program or plan shall, upon written request, have access to—\n“(1)\n any records relating to such employee’s drug test; and\n“(2)\n any records relating to the results of any relevant certification, review, or revocation-of-certification proceedings, as referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii)(III).\n“(e)\n The results of a drug test of a Federal employee may not be disclosed without the prior written consent of such employee, unless the disclosure would be—\n“(1)\n to the employee’s medical review official (as defined in the scientific and technical guidelines referred to in subsection (a)(1)(A)(ii));\n“(2)\n to the administrator of any Employee Assistance Program in which the employee is receiving counseling or treatment or is otherwise participating;\n“(3)\n to any supervisory or management official within the employee’s agency having authority to take the adverse personnel action against such employee; or\n“(4)\n pursuant to the order of a court of competent jurisdiction where required by the United States Government to defend against any challenge against any adverse personnel action.\n“(f)\n [Terminated, effective May 15, 2000, see section 3003 of Pub. L. 104–66, as amended, set out as a note under section 1113 of Title 31, Money and Finance, and page 151 of House Document No. 103–7.]\n“(g)\n For purposes of this section, the terms ‘agency’ and ‘Employee Assistance Program’ each has the meaning given such term under section 7(b) of Executive Order Numbered 12564 [set out as a note below], as in effect on September 15, 1986.”\n[For abolition of United States Information Agency (other than Broadcasting Board of Governors and International Broadcasting Bureau), transfer of functions, and treatment of references thereto, see sections 6531, 6532, and 6551 of Title 22, Foreign Relations and Intercourse.]\nLimitation on Gratuities at Naval Shipbuilding Ceremonies\nPub. L. 99–145, title XIV, § 1461, Nov. 8, 1985, 99 Stat. 765, provided that:\n“(a)\n General Rule.—\nA Federal officer, employee, or Member of Congress may not accept, directly or indirectly, any tangible thing of value as a gift or memento in connection with a ceremony to mark the completion of a naval shipbuilding milestone.\n“(b)\n Exclusion.—\nSubsection (a) does not apply to a gift or memento that has a value of less than $100.\n“(c)\n Definitions.—\nFor purposes of this section, the terms ‘officer’, ‘employee’, and ‘Member of Congress’ have the meanings given those terms in sections 2104, 2105, and 2106, respectively, of title 5, United States Code.”\nExecutive Documents\nEmergency Preparedness Functions\nFor assignment of certain emergency preparedness functions to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, see Parts 1, 2, and 22 of Ex. Ord. No. 12656, Nov. 18, 1988, 53 F.R. 47491, set out as a note under section 5195 of Title 42, The Public Health and Welfare.\nDesignation of Director of the Bureau of the Budget as Member of Federal Labor Relations Council\nPresidential Order of December 8, 1969, provided that:\nPursuant to the provisions of section 4 of Executive Order 11491 [set out as a note under this section], I hereby designate the Director of the Bureau of the Budget [now the Office of Management and Budget] as a member of the Federal Labor Relations Council. This order of designation shall be published in the Federal Register.\nRichard Nixon.\nExecutive Order No. 9845\nEx. Ord. No. 9845, Apr. 28, 1947, 12 F.R. 2799, which permitted Bureau of Reclamation employees to accept appointments as constables or deputy sheriffs under state or territorial laws, was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 11408, Apr. 25, 1968, 33 F.R. 6459.\nEx. Ord. No. 12564. Drug-Free Federal Workplace\nEx. Ord. No. 12564, Sept. 15, 1986, 51 F.R. 32889, provided:\nI, RONALD REAGAN, President of the United States of America, find that:\nDrug use is having serious adverse effects upon a significant proportion of the national work force and results in billions of dollars of lost productivity each year;\nThe Federal government, as an employer, is concerned with the well-being of its employees, the successful accomplishment of agency missions, and the need to maintain employee productivity;\nThe Federal government, as the largest employer in the Nation, can and should show the way towards achieving drug-free workplaces through a program designed to offer drug users a helping hand and, at the same time, demonstrating to drug users and potential drug users that drugs will not be tolerated in the Federal workplace;\nThe profits from illegal drugs provide the single greatest source of income for organized crime, fuel violent street crime, and otherwise contribute to the breakdown of our society;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees is inconsistent not only with the law-abiding behavior expected of all citizens, but also with the special trust placed in such employees as servants of the public;\nFederal employees who use illegal drugs, on or off duty, tend to be less productive, less reliable, and prone to greater absenteeism than their fellow employees who do not use illegal drugs;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees impairs the efficiency of Federal departments and agencies, undermines public confidence in them, and makes it more difficult for other employees who do not use illegal drugs to perform their jobs effectively. The use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees also can pose a serious health and safety threat to members of the public and to other Federal employees;\nThe use of illegal drugs, on or off duty, by Federal employees in certain positions evidences less than the complete reliability, stability, and good judgment that is consistent with access to sensitive information and creates the possibility of coercion, influence, and irresponsible action under pressure that may pose a serious risk to national security, the public safety, and the effective enforcement of the law; and\nFederal employees who use illegal drugs must themselves be primarily responsible for changing their behavior and, if necessary, begin the process of rehabilitating themselves.\nBy the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the United States of America, including section 3301(2) of Title 5 of the United States Code, section 7301 of Title 5 of the United States Code, section 290ee–1 of Title 42 of the United States Code, deeming such action in the best interests of national security, public health and safety, law enforcement and the efficiency of the Federal service, and in order to establish standards and procedures to ensure fairness in achieving a drug-free Federal workplace and to protect the privacy of Federal employees, it is hereby ordered as follows:","sections_touched":["section 3003","section 1113","section 7(b)","sections 6531","sections 2104","Parts 1","section 5195","section 4","section 3301(2)","section 7301","section 290"],"signing_date":"1986-09-15","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:12564","page_or_item":"5 U.S.C. 7301","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"ed3ba438ffd040def329beea813ce0a7382027b9103dd5a39c0d4b489110239e","signing_date":"1986-09-15","text_path":"jobs/theophilus-sources/output/texts/usc-t5-s7301.txt","text_sha256":"ed3ba438ffd040def329beea813ce0a7382027b9103dd5a39c0d4b489110239e","url":"https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title5-section7301&num=0&edition=prelim"},"verb":"terminate"}],"generic_refs_excluded":234,"id":"CHAIN:EO:11491","notes":"Named, located change provisions only; July 20, 2012; APP node 302041; common-crawl capture 2025-11-11T20:49:23Z","requires_page_check":true,"sha256":"137dc9034192b4f99c431813ea7d42bf14dfd00531a9204c7feb5c31d0f77030","signing_date":"2012-07-20","text_path":"jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-13620-taking-additional-steps-address-the-national-emergency-with-respect.txt","text_sha256":"81c0932eda3a4963d6983ed7378d624d764b438a423a184abe60031605aa4701","url":"https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-13620-taking-additional-steps-address-the-national-emergency-with-respect"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:13620","char_end":3858,"char_start":1207,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:13536#2","notes":"Change wording lead; chronology does not decide legal effect.","provision_text":"Section 1(a) of Executive Order 13536 is hereby amended to\nread as follows:\n‘‘(a) All property and interests in property that are in the United States,\nthat hereafter come within the United States, or that are or hereafter come\nwithin the possession or control of any United States person, including\nany foreign branch, of the following persons are blocked and may not\nbe transferred, paid, exported, withdrawn or otherwise dealt in:\n(i) the persons listed in the Annex to this order; and\n(ii) any person determined by the Secretary of the Treasury, in consultation\nwith the Secretary of State:\n(A) to have engaged in acts that directly or indirectly threaten the peace,\nsecurity, or stability of Somalia, including but not limited to:\n(1) acts that threaten the Djibouti Agreement of August 18, 2008, or the\npolitical process;\n(2) acts that threaten the Transitional Federal Institutions or future Somali\ngoverning institutions, the African Union Mission in Somalia (AMISOM),\nor other future international peacekeeping operations related to Somalia;\nor\n(3) acts to misappropriate Somali public assets;\n(B) to have obstructed the delivery of humanitarian assistance to Somalia,\nor access to, or distribution of, humanitarian assistance in Somalia;\n(C) to have directly or indirectly supplied, sold, or transferred to Somalia,\nor to have been the recipient in the territory of Somalia of, arms or any\nrelated materiel, or any technical advice, training or assistance, including\nfinancing and financial assistance, related to military activities;\n(D) to be responsible for or complicit in, or responsible for ordering,\ncontrolling, or otherwise directing, or to have participated in, the commission\nof acts of violence targeting civilians in Somalia, including killing and\nmaiming, sexual and gender-based violence, attacks on schools and hospitals,\ntaking hostages, and forced displacement;\n(E) to be a political or military leader recruiting or using children in\narmed conflict in Somalia;\n(F) to have engaged, directly or indirectly, in the import or export of\ncharcoal from Somalia on or after February 22, 2012;\n(G) to have materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material,\nlogistical or technical support for, or goods or services in support of, the\nactivities described in subsections (a)(ii)(A) through (F) of this section or\nany person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant\nto this order; or\n(H) to be owned or controlled by, or to have acted or purported to\nact for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, any person whose property\nand interests in property are blocked pursuant to this order.’’\nSec. 2.","sections_touched":["Section 1(a)"],"signing_date":"2012-07-20","source":{"acceptable_as_original":false,"filing_date":null,"grade":"held_text_lead","instrument_id":"EO:13620","page_or_item":"77 FR 43483-43485 (PDF pp. 1-3)","requires_page_check":false,"sha256":"6c5632c04a9294befa74c7f9248fe9b92c458ed7503a78a318154b609875fa9d","signing_date":"2012-07-20","text_path":"jobs/clause-drafts/output/texts/cd-stage21-13620-6c5632c04a.txt","text_sha256":"8abdea75447738b882af060ba04dbb4bb131cbda1960665a331c3859e7e74ebd","url":"https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2012-07-24/pdf/2012-18237.pdf"},"verb":"amend"},{"actor_id":"EO:13620","char_end":4805,"char_start":1834,"confidence":"medium","how_named":"direct","id":"CHAIN:EO:13536#3","notes":"Change wording lead; - **ACT:EO:12657>EO:13286**; Sd3145c7b44424f882132e4cb; {"actor_id":"EO:13286","char_end":25827,"char_start":25648,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2501,"char_start":2411,"text":"Executive Order 13260 of March 19, 2002, is hereby revoked effective as of March 31, 2003."},{"char_end":41701,"char_start":40943,"text":"(a)\nin the case of the Department of Defense, the Secretary of Defense has, after consideration of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002, determined that the exercise of authority under this order is necessary for the timely and effective conduct of United States military or intelligence activities; and\n(b)\nin the case of any other executive department or agency that has authority under this order, (i) the Secretary of Homeland Security has advised whether the use of the authority provided under subtitle G of title VIII of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 would be appropriate, and (ii) the Director of the Office and Management and Budget has approved the exercise of authority under this order.\"."},{"char_end":49577,"char_start":49526,"text":"This order shall become effective on March 1, 2003."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12657>EO:13286","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 41.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":["Without prejudice to subsections (a) through (i) of this section, all responsibilities assigned to specific Federal officials pursuant to Executive Order 12656 that are substantially the same as any responsibility assigned to, or function transferred to, the Secretary of Homeland Security pursuant to the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (regardless of whether such responsibility or function is expressly required to be carried out through another official of the Department of Homeland Security or not pursuant to such Act), or intended or required to be carried out by an agency or an agency component transferred to the Department of Homeland Security pursuant to such Act, are hereby reassigned to the Secretary of Homeland Security.","Executive Order 11239 of July 31, 1965 (\"Enforcement of the Convention for Safety of Life at Sea, 1960\"), as amended, is further amended, without prejudice to section 1–106 of Executive Order 12234 of September 3, 1980 (\"Enforcement of the Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea\"), by:","Savings Provision."],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2003-02-28","target_id":"EO:12657","verb":"amend"}

- **ACT:EO:11589>EO:12148@ec987afa5120a1e5**; Sd5c06180aa75296f92dffed2; {"actor_id":"EO:12148","char_end":15488,"char_start":11674,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":7159,"char_start":6707,"text":"In order that civil defense planning continues to be fully compatible \nwith the Nation’s overall strategic policy, and in order to maintain an effective \nlink between strategic nuclear planning and nuclear attack preparedness \nplanning, the development of civil defense policies and programs by the \nDirector of the Federal Emergency Management Agency shall be subject to \noversight by the Secretary of Defense and the National Security Council.\n2-205."},{"char_end":23802,"char_start":23765,"text":"This Order is effective July 15,1979."}],"exceptions_text":["to the extent transferred to the President by \nReorganization Plan No","except those functions vested in the \nPresident by Sections 301(relating to the declaration of emergencies and major \ndisasters), 401 (relating to the repair, reconstruction, restoration, or replace­\nment of Federal facilities), and 409 (relating to food coupons and surplus \ncommodities), are hereby delegated to the Director of the Federal Emergency \nManagement Agency"],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:11589>EO:12148@ec987afa5120a1e5","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Section 4.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"1979-07-20","target_id":"EO:11589","verb":"transfer"}

  Text: [Ta798875b457fdfc5cbafe5e1](#ta798875b457fdfc5cbafe5e1); absolute characters 923–1106
- **ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381**; Sbc567c32bbf28f21bd975468; {"actor_id":"EO:13381","char_end":9098,"char_start":8942,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1469,"char_start":1102,"text":"To the extent consistent with safeguarding the security \nof the United States and protecting classified national security information \nfrom unauthorized disclosure, agency functions relating to determining eligi-\nbility for access to classified national security information shall be appro-\npriately uniform, centralized, efficient, effective, timely, and reciprocal."},{"char_end":4300,"char_start":1529,"text":"The Director \nof the Office of Management and Budget (Director): \n(a) may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy set forth \nin section 1 of this order, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of \nany agency (solely or jointly) any process relating to determinations of \neligibility for access to classified national security information, with the \nagency’s exercise of such assigned process to be subject to the Director’s \nsupervision and to such terms and conditions (including approval by the \nOffice of Management and Budget) as the Director determines appropriate; \n(b) shall carry out any process that the Director does not assign to another \nagency (or agencies) under subsection (a); \n(c) may, after consultation with the Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, \nthe Attorney General, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Homeland \nSecurity, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), and the Director of \nthe Office of Personnel Management, issue guidelines and instructions to \nthe heads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, effi-\nciency, effectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to determinations \nby agencies of eligibility for access to classified national security information; \n(d) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to Sensitive \nCompartmented Information (SCI) and ‘‘special access programs pertaining \nto intelligence activities; including special activities, but not including mili-\ntary operational, strategic, and tactical programs’’ (Intelligence SAPs) under \nsection 4.3(a) of Executive Order 12958 of April 17, 1995, as amended, \nissue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the DNI to the \nheads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in making such determinations relating to those \nprograms; \n(e) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to special access \nprograms (SAP) as defined in Executive Order 12958 other than Intelligence \nSAPs, issue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the agency \nhead with responsibility for the SAP to ensure appropriate uniformity, cen-\ntralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and timeliness in making such deter-\nminations relating to those programs; \n(f) may report periodically to the President on implementation by agencies \nof the policy set forth in section 1; and \nVerDate jul<14>2003 16:49 Jun 29, 2005 Jkt 205001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\30JNE0.SGM 30JNE0\n=== PDF page 2 of 3 ===\n37954 Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 125 / Thursday, June 30, 2005 / Presidential Documents \n(g) shall submit reports to the Congress relating to the subject matter \nof this order to the extent required by law."},{"char_end":8124,"char_start":6366,"text":"(b) the term ‘‘classified national security information ’’ means information \nthat is classified pursuant to Executive Order 12958; \n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (iv) ensuring reciprocal recognition of determinations of \neligibility for access to classified information among the agencies of the \nUnited States Government, including resolution of disputes involving the \nreciprocity of security clearances and access to SCI and SAPs; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9762,"char_start":9469,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 5.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2005-06-27","target_id":"EO:12171","verb":"amend"}

\n(e) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to special access \nprograms (SAP) as defined in Executive Order 12958 other than Intelligence \nSAPs, issue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the agency \nhead with responsibility for the SAP to ensure appropriate uniformity, cen-\ntralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and timeliness in making such deter-\nminations relating to those programs; \n(f) may report periodically to the President on implementation by agencies \nof the policy set forth in section 1; and \nVerDate jul<14>2003 16:49 Jun 29, 2005 Jkt 205001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\30JNE0.SGM 30JNE0\n=== PDF page 2 of 3 ===\n37954 Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 125 / Thursday, June 30, 2005 / Presidential Documents \n(g) shall submit reports to the Congress relating to the subject matter \nof this order to the extent required by law."},{"char_end":8124,"char_start":6366,"text":"(b) the term ‘‘classified national security information ’’ means information \nthat is classified pursuant to Executive Order 12958; \n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (iv) ensuring reciprocal recognition of determinations of \neligibility for access to classified information among the agencies of the \nUnited States Government, including resolution of disputes involving the \nreciprocity of security clearances and access to SCI and SAPs; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9762,"char_start":9469,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381@4b13f4080de3eb38","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only;   Text: [Tfa89da4868862ae408ae0857](#tfa89da4868862ae408ae0857); absolute characters 7588–7740
- **ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381@b2e840b54d87fbe8**; Sbc567c32bbf28f21bd975468; {"actor_id":"EO:13381","char_end":9098,"char_start":8942,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1469,"char_start":1102,"text":"To the extent consistent with safeguarding the security \nof the United States and protecting classified national security information \nfrom unauthorized disclosure, agency functions relating to determining eligi-\nbility for access to classified national security information shall be appro-\npriately uniform, centralized, efficient, effective, timely, and reciprocal."},{"char_end":4300,"char_start":1529,"text":"The Director \nof the Office of Management and Budget (Director): \n(a) may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy set forth \nin section 1 of this order, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of \nany agency (solely or jointly) any process relating to determinations of \neligibility for access to classified national security information, with the \nagency’s exercise of such assigned process to be subject to the Director’s \nsupervision and to such terms and conditions (including approval by the \nOffice of Management and Budget) as the Director determines appropriate; \n(b) shall carry out any process that the Director does not assign to another \nagency (or agencies) under subsection (a); \n(c) may, after consultation with the Secretary of State, Secretary of Defense, \nthe Attorney General, the Secretary of Energy, the Secretary of Homeland \nSecurity, the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), and the Director of \nthe Office of Personnel Management, issue guidelines and instructions to \nthe heads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, effi-\nciency, effectiveness, and timeliness in processes relating to determinations \nby agencies of eligibility for access to classified national security information; \n(d) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to Sensitive \nCompartmented Information (SCI) and ‘‘special access programs pertaining \nto intelligence activities; including special activities, but not including mili-\ntary operational, strategic, and tactical programs’’ (Intelligence SAPs) under \nsection 4.3(a) of Executive Order 12958 of April 17, 1995, as amended, \nissue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the DNI to the \nheads of agencies to ensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, \neffectiveness, and timeliness in making such determinations relating to those \nprograms; \n(e) may, with regard to determining eligibility for access to special access \nprograms (SAP) as defined in Executive Order 12958 other than Intelligence \nSAPs, issue guidelines and instructions with the concurrence of the agency \nhead with responsibility for the SAP to ensure appropriate uniformity, cen-\ntralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and timeliness in making such deter-\nminations relating to those programs; \n(f) may report periodically to the President on implementation by agencies \nof the policy set forth in section 1; and \nVerDate jul<14>2003 16:49 Jun 29, 2005 Jkt 205001 PO 00000 Frm 00003 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\30JNE0.SGM 30JNE0\n=== PDF page 2 of 3 ===\n37954 Federal Register / Vol. 70, No. 125 / Thursday, June 30, 2005 / Presidential Documents \n(g) shall submit reports to the Congress relating to the subject matter \nof this order to the extent required by law."},{"char_end":8124,"char_start":6366,"text":"(b) the term ‘‘classified national security information ’’ means information \nthat is classified pursuant to Executive Order 12958; \n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (iv) ensuring reciprocal recognition of determinations of \neligibility for access to classified information among the agencies of the \nUnited States Government, including resolution of disputes involving the \nreciprocity of security clearances and access to SCI and SAPs; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9762,"char_start":9469,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381@b2e840b54d87fbe8","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 5.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2005-06-27","target_id":"EO:12171","verb":"amend"}

\n(c) the term ‘‘counterintelligence’’ has the meaning specified for that term \nin section 3 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 401a); and \n(d) the term ‘‘process’’ means: (i) oversight of determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified national security information, including for SCI and \nSAPs made by any agency, as well as the acquisition of information through \ninvestigation or other means upon which such determinations are made; \n(ii) developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of access \neligibility determinations, to include for SAPs; (iii) designating an authorized \nagency for making access eligibility determinations and an authorized agency \nfor collecting information through investigation upon which such determina-\ntions are made; (v) ensuring \nthe availability of resources to achieve clearance and investigative program \ngoals regarding the making of access determinations as well as the collection \nof information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made; and (vi) developing tools and techniques for en-\nhancing the making of access eligibility determinations as well as the collec-\ntion of information through investigation and other means upon which such \ndeterminations are made."},{"char_end":9157,"char_start":8864,"text":"(d) Existing delegations of authority to any agency relating to granting \naccess to classified information and conducting investigations shall remain \nin effect, subject to the authority of the Office of Management and Budget \nunder section 2 of this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13381@d1aa7d324cd74e14","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only;   Text: [T5092b4d9c923c39e598d098d](#t5092b4d9c923c39e598d098d); absolute characters 8337–8493
- **ACT:EO:12171>EO:13467**; S023de79d8eb490afcb428b20; {"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":19622,"char_start":19082,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1951,"char_start":1347,"text":"Executive branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, \naccess to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligi-\nbility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and \nshall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity."},{"char_end":8369,"char_start":7558,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and \nmethods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabili-\nties and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that \nrelevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 3 of 6 ===\n38105 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nrapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, pro-\ntecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the \nnational interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \nworkforce."},{"char_end":11953,"char_start":11412,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy \nset forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with \nlaw, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or \njointly) any function within the Council ’s responsibility relating to alignment \nand improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, con-\ntractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility \nfor access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":12890,"char_start":12501,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director \nof the Office of Personnel Management will continue to be responsible \nfor developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investiga-\ntions and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility \nfor logical and physical access."},{"char_end":15137,"char_start":12980,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations and determinations of eligi-\nbility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive \nposition made by any agency; \n(ii) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion \nof investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iii) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies to \nensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and \ntimeliness in processes relating to determinations by agencies of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iv) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto conduct investigations of persons who are proposed for access to classi-\nfied information to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria \nfor obtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position; \n(v) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information in accordance \nwith Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995; \n(vi) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to classified \ninformation among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and determinations of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; and \n(vii) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (vi), above, with \nthe agency ’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject to the \nSecurity Executive Agent ’s oversight and with such terms and conditions \n(including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the Security Execu-\ntive Agent determines appropriate."},{"char_end":20366,"char_start":19744,"text":"VerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 6 of 6 ===\n38108 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \n(g) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 \nof June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility \nfor access to classified information and conducting investigations shall 13 \nremain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this \norder to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13467","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2008-06-30","target_id":"EO:12171","verb":"amend"}

{"actor_id":"EO:13467","char_end":17493,"char_start":17261,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":1110,"char_start":515,"text":"Executive branch policies and procedures relating to suitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, access to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligibility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent standards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and shall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national interest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal Government relies to conduct our Nation's business and protect national security."},{"char_end":6965,"char_start":6435,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and methods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabilities and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that relevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared rapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, protecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the national interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective workforce."},{"char_end":10582,"char_start":10049,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy set forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with law, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or jointly) any function within the Council's responsibility relating to alignment and improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility for access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":11238,"char_start":10856,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director of the Office of Personnel Management will continue to be responsible for developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility for logical and physical access."},{"char_end":11869,"char_start":11555,"text":"(ii)          shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies and procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position;"},{"char_end":18276,"char_start":17930,"text":"(g) Existing delegations of authority made pursuant to Executive Order 13381 of June 27, 2005, as amended, to any agency relating to granting eligibility for access to classified information and conducting investigations shall 13 remain in effect, subject to the exercise of authorities pursuant to this order to revise or revoke such delegation."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13467@aa56b7e82df98ecc","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sensitive position, \naccess to federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligi-\nbility for access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent \nstandards to the extent possible, provide for reciprocal recognition, and \nshall ensure cost-effective, timely,and efficient protection of the national \ninterest, while providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal \nGovernment relies to conduct our Nation’s business and protect national \nsecurity."},{"char_end":8369,"char_start":7558,"text":"(b) The aligned system shall employ updated and consistent standards and \nmethods, enable innovations with enterprise information technology capabili-\nties and end-to-end automation to the extent practicable, and ensure that \nrelevant information maintained by agencies can be accessed and shared \nVerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00004 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76 with PROPOSALS2\n=== PDF page 3 of 6 ===\n38105 Federal Register / Vol. 73, No. 128 / Wednesday, July 2, 2008 / Presidential Documents \nrapidly across the executive branch, while protecting national security, pro-\ntecting privacy-related information, ensuring resulting decisions are in the \nnational interest, and providing the Federal Government with an effective \nworkforce."},{"char_end":11953,"char_start":11412,"text":"(e) The Chair may, to ensure the effective implementation of the policy \nset forth in section 1.1 of this order and to the extent consistent with \nlaw, assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely or \njointly) any function within the Council ’s responsibility relating to alignment \nand improvement of investigations and determinations of suitability, con-\ntractor employee fitness, eligibility for logical and physical access, eligibility \nfor access to classified information, or eligibility to hold a sensitive position."},{"char_end":12890,"char_start":12501,"text":"As the Suitability Executive Agent, the Director \nof the Office of Personnel Management will continue to be responsible \nfor developing and implementing uniform and consistent policies and proce-\ndures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion of investiga-\ntions and adjudications relating to determinations of suitability and eligibility \nfor logical and physical access."},{"char_end":15137,"char_start":12980,"text":"The Security Executive Agent: \n(i) shall direct the oversight of investigations and determinations of eligi-\nbility for access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive \nposition made by any agency; \n(ii) shall be responsible for developing uniform and consistent policies \nand procedures to ensure the effective, efficient, and timely completion \nof investigations and adjudications relating to determinations of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iii) may issue guidelines and instructions to the heads of agencies to \nensure appropriate uniformity, centralization, efficiency, effectiveness, and \ntimeliness in processes relating to determinations by agencies of eligibility \nfor access to classified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; \n(iv) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto conduct investigations of persons who are proposed for access to classi-\nfied information to ascertain whether such persons satisfy the criteria \nfor obtaining and retaining access to classified information or eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position; \n(v) shall serve as the final authority to designate an agency or agencies \nto determine eligibility for access to classified information in accordance \nwith Executive Order 12968 of August 2, 1995; \n(vi) shall ensure reciprocal recognition of eligibility for access to classified \ninformation among the agencies, including acting as the final authority \nto arbitrate and resolve disputes among the agencies involving the reci-\nprocity of investigations and determinations of eligibility for access to \nclassified information or eligibility to hold a sensitive position; and \n(vii) may assign, in whole or in part, to the head of any agency (solely \nor jointly) any of the functions detailed in (i) through (vi), above, with \nthe agency ’s exercise of such assigned functions to be subject to the \nSecurity Executive Agent ’s oversight and with such terms and conditions \n(including approval by the Security Executive Agent) as the Security Execu-\ntive Agent determines appropriate."},{"char_end":20366,"char_start":19744,"text":"VerDate Aug<31>2005 18:32 Jul 01, 2008 Jkt 214001 PO 00000 Frm 00007 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\02JYE0.SGM 02JYE0hsrobinson on PROD1PC76   Text: [T294d8ffd439380269383d172](#t294d8ffd439380269383d172); absolute characters 4846–4978
- **ACT:EO:12171>EO:13741**; S713e37627cbcf641a4177b39; {"actor_id":"EO:13741","char_end":11733,"char_start":11441,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"unknown","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":2426,"char_start":1744,"text":"Policy: Executive branch policies and procedures relating to \nsuitability, contractor or Federal employee fitness, eligibility to hold a sen-\nsitive position, authorization to be issued a Federal credential for access \nto federally controlled facilities and information systems, and eligibility \nfor access to classified information shall be aligned using consistent standards \nto the extent possible, shall provide for reciprocal recognition, and shall \nensure cost-effective, timely, and efficient protection of the national interest, \nwhile providing fair treatment to those upon whom the Federal Government \nrelies to conduct the Nation’s business and protect national security."},{"char_end":3170,"char_start":2864,"text":"To help fulfill \nthese responsibilities, there shall be a primary executive branch investigative \nservice provider whose mission is to provide effective, efficient, and secure \nbackground investigations for the Federal Government.’’ \n(c) Sections 1.3(k) and (l) are redesignated as sections 1.3(l) and (m)."},{"char_end":3801,"char_start":3172,"text":"(d) A new section 1.3(k) is added to read as follows: ‘‘(k) ‘‘National \nBackground Investigations Bureau’’ (NBIB) means the National Background \nInvestigations Bureau, established within the Office of Personnel Management \nwith responsibility for conducting effective, efficient, and secure personnel \nbackground investigations pursuant to law, rule, regulation, or Executive \nOrder.’’ \n(e) Section 2.2(b) is amended to read as follows: \n‘‘(b) The Deputy Director for Management, Office of Management and \nBudget, shall serve as Chair of the Council and shall have authority, direction, \nand control over the Council’s functions."},{"char_end":7172,"char_start":5028,"text":"(a) The National Background Investigations Bureau shall: \n‘‘(1) serve as the primary executive branch service provider for back-\nground investigations for eligibility for access to classified information; \neligibility to hold a sensitive position; suitability or, for employees in \npositions not subject to suitability, fitness for Government employment; \nfitness to perform work for or on behalf of the Government as a contractor \nemployee; and authorization to be issued a Federal credential for logical \nand physical access to federally controlled facilities and information sys-\ntems; \n‘‘(2) provide effective, efficient, and secure personnel background inves-\ntigations for the Federal Government; \n‘‘(3) provide the Council information, to the extent permitted by law, \non matters of performance, timeliness, capacity, information technology \nmodernization, continuous performance improvement, and other relevant \naspects of NBIB operations; \n‘‘(4) be headquartered in or near Washington, District of Columbia; \n‘‘(5) have dedicated resources, including but not limited to a senior \nprivacy official; \n‘‘(6) institutionalize interagency collaboration and take advantage of ex-\npertise across the executive branch; \n‘‘(7) continuously improve investigative operations, emphasizing infor-\nmation accuracy and protection, and regularly integrate best practices, \nincluding those identified by subject matter experts from industry, aca-\ndemia, or other relevant sources; \n‘‘(8) conduct personnel background investigations in accordance with \nuniform and consistent policies, procedures, standards, and requirements \nestablished by the Security Executive Agent and the Suitability Executive \nAgent; and \n‘‘(9) conduct other personnel background investigations as authorized \nby law, rule, regulation, or Executive Order. \n‘‘(b) The Secretary of Defense shall design, develop, deploy, operate, secure, \ndefend, and continuously update and modernize, as necessary, background \ninvestigation information technology systems that support all Federal back-\nground investigation processes conducted by the National Background Inves-\ntigations Bureau."},{"char_end":8129,"char_start":7494,"text":"The Secretary of Defense shall operate the \ndatabase in the information technology systems containing appropriate data \nrelevant to the granting, denial, or revocation of a security clearance or \naccess pertaining to military, civilian, or Government contractor personnel, \nsee 50 U.S.C. 3341(e), consistent with and following an explicit delegation \nfrom the Director of the Office of Personnel Management pursuant to 5 \nU.S.C. 1104. \n‘‘(c) Delegations and designations of investigative authority in place on \nthe date of establishment of the National Background Investigations Bureau \nshall remain in effect until amended or revoked."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13741","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective wording is ambiguous, section-specific, or has no determinable date.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2016-09-29","target_id":"EO:12171","verb":"amend"}

- **ACT:EO:12171>EO:13869**; S3f9ba07a5c9530d1b7c27055; {"actor_id":"EO:13869","char_end":21524,"char_start":21394,"confidence":"medium","effective_class":"agency_variable","effective_date":null,"effective_wording":[{"char_end":7887,"char_start":4503,"text":"The Secretary of Defense may rename the \nDCSA and reassign any of its responsibilities to another Department of \nDefense component or components, provided, however, that the Secretary \nof Defense shall consult with the Directors of National Intelligence, the \nOffice of Personnel Management, and the Office of Management and Budget \nbefore renaming the DCSA or reassigning the responsibilities specified \nin section 2.6(b)(ii) and (iv) of this order to another Department of Defense \ncomponent.’’ \n‘‘(ii) Pursuant to and consistent with section 3001(c) of the Intelligence \nReform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (50 U.S.C. 3341(c)), sections \n925(a)(1) and (d)(2) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal \nYear 2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note), and in accordance with subsection (d) \nof this section, no later than June 24, 2019, the DCSA shall serve as \nthe primary entity for conducting effective, efficient, and secure background \ninvestigations for the Federal Government for determining whether covered \nindividuals are or continue to be eligible for access to classified information \nor eligible to hold a sensitive position.’’ \n‘‘(iii) Pursuant to and consistent with sections 925(a)(1) and (d)(2) of \nthe National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (10 U.S.C. \n1564 note) and in accordance with subsection (d) of this section, no \nlater than June 24, 2019, the DCSA shall serve as the primary entity \nfor conducting effective, efficient, and secure background investigations \nfor determining the suitability or, for employees in positions not subject \nto suitability, fitness for Department of Defense employment; fitness to \nperform work for or on behalf of the Department of Defense as a contractor; \nfitness to work as a nonappropriated fund employee, as defined in Execu-\ntive Order 13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; and authorization \nto be issued a Federal credential for logical and physical access to facilities \nor information systems controlled by the Department of Defense.’’ \n‘‘(iv) Consistent with and following an explicit delegation from the Director \nof the Office of Personnel Management pursuant to section 1104 of title \n5, United States Code, and consistent with subsection (e) of this section, \nno later than June 24, 2019, the DCSA shall serve as the primary entity \nfor conducting effective, efficient, and secure background investigations \nfor the Federal Government not described in subsections (b)(ii) and (b)(iii) \nof this section, for determining suitability or, for employees in positions \nnot subject to suitability, fitness for Government employment; fitness to \nperform work for or on behalf of the Government as a contractor; fitness \nto work as a nonappropriated fund employee, as defined in Executive \nOrder 13488 of January 16, 2009, as amended; and authorization to be \nissued a Federal credential for logical and physical access to federally \ncontrolled facilities or information systems.’’ \n‘‘(v) The DCSA shall conduct other background investigations as authorized \nby law, designation, rule, regulation, or Executive Order.’’ \n‘‘(vi) The DCSA shall provide information to the Council established by \nsection 2.4 of this order regarding matters of performance, including timeli-\nness and continuous improvement, capacity, information technology mod-\nernization, and other relevant aspects of its operations."},{"char_end":13910,"char_start":9772,"text":"The Secretary \nof Defense shall operate the database in the information technology systems \ncontaining appropriate data relevant to the granting, denial, or revocation \nof eligibility for access to classified information or eligibility for a sensitive \nposition pertaining to military, civilian, or Government contractor per-\nsonnel, see section 3341(e) of title 50, United States Code, consistent \nwith, as applicable, an explicit delegation from the Director of the Office \nof Personnel Management pursuant to section 1104 of title 5, United \nStates Code.’’ \n‘‘(viii) The Secretary of Defense shall, by June 24, 2019, execute a written \nagreement with the Director of the Office of Personnel Management desig-\nnating the appropriate support functions to be transferred as part of the \ninvestigative mission, consistent with section 925(d)(2)(B) of the National \nDefense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note), \nand setting forth expectations for the transition period, including for detail-\ning personnel, funding background investigations, using and safeguarding \ninformation technology, managing facilities and property, contracting, ad-\nministrative support, records access, and addressing any claims.’’ \n‘‘(ix) The Secretary of Defense shall, upon finalization of the agreement \ndescribed in paragraph (viii) of this subsection and in accordance with \nits terms: \n(A) establish the Personnel Vetting Transformation Office within the \nDepartment of Defense, which will include personnel from the Department \nof Defense and other stakeholder agencies, as appropriate; and \n(B) commence efforts to receive transferred or delegated functions and, \nas appropriate, associated Office of Personnel Management operations, \nresources, and personnel, to the DCSA.’’ \n‘‘(x) The Secretary of Defense shall: \n(A) no later than June 24, 2019, and every 180 days thereafter until \nthe transfer is complete, provide a report to the President, in coordination \nwith the Director of the Office of Personnel Management and through \nthe Director of the Office of Management and Budget, regarding the status \nof the transfer, including any resource or funding shortfall and gaps in \nauthority; \n(B) take necessary actions to enable the Department of Defense to receive \nany resources, including personnel, made available as a result of subsection \n(d) of this section; and \n(C) notify the President upon completion of the transition period.’’ \n‘‘(xi) In the event the agreement described in paragraph (viii) of this \nsubsection and section 2.6(e)(v) of this order is not executed by June \n24, 2019, beginning on such date, the Secretary of Defense shall begin \nto take necessary actions to begin execution of paragraph (ix) until the \nagreement described in paragraph (viii) of this subsection is executed, \nat which time the Secretary of Defense shall ensure actions subject to \nsuch agreement under paragraph (ix) of this subsection are executed in \naccordance with its terms.’’ \n(d) Section 2.6(c) of Executive Order 13467 is revised to read as follows: \n‘‘(c) Existing delegations of authority to conduct background investigations \nmade by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management, as the \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 18:02 Apr 26, 2019 Jkt 247001 PO 00000 Frm 00005 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\29APE0.SGM 29APE0khammond on DSKBBV9HB2PROD with PRES DOC\n=== PDF page 4 of 7 ===\n18128 Federal Register / Vol. 84, No. 82 / Monday, April 29, 2019 / Presidential Documents \nSuitability and Credentialing Executive Agent or as otherwise authorized \nby statute or Executive Order, to any agency relating to suitability, fitness, \nor credentialing determinations, existing designations made by the Director \nof National Intelligence, as the Security Executive Agent or as otherwise \nauthorized by statute or Executive Order, relating to investigating persons \nwho are proposed for access to classified information or for eligibility \nto hold a sensitive position, or existing delegations of authority to conduct \nbackground investigations made by the President to any other agency \nthrough any Executive Order shall remain in effect."},{"char_end":20598,"char_start":15043,"text":"The transfer shall \ncommence no later than June 24, 2019, and shall: \n(i) be executed with the assistance of the Personnel Vetting Trans-\nformation Office established pursuant to paragraph (b)(ix) of this section, \nwhich shall, in providing such assistance, consider input from other stake-\nholder agencies, as appropriate; \n(ii) be conducted in accordance with a risk management approach that \nis consistent with Office of Management and Budget Circular A–123; \n(iii) include any appropriate funds that the Secretary of Defense and \nthe Director of the Office of Personnel Management, with the concurrence \nof the Director of the Office of Management and Budget, determine to \nbe available and necessary to finance and discharge the functions trans-\nferred; \n(iv) be consistent with the transition from legacy information technology \nas required by subsection (b)(vii) of this section; \n(v) build upon the implementation plan developed pursuant to section \n951(a)(1) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 \n(Public Law 114–328), which is being implemented pursuant to section \n925 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2018 (10 \nU.S.C. 1564 note); and \n(vi) permit NBIB to conduct background investigations for DCSA, as \nnecessary, until September 30, 2019.’’ \n‘‘(e) The Director of the Office of Personnel Management shall: \n(i) no later than June 24, 2019, take any steps necessary to make effective \nthe delegation, pursuant to section 1104(a)(2) of title 5, United States \nCode, of the functions described in subsection (b)(iv) of this section; \n(ii) promptly establish appropriate performance standards and oversight \nas required by section 1104(b) of title 5, United States Code; \n(iii) work in coordination with the Secretary of Defense to reassign \nappropriate resources, including personnel, to the DCSA and provide all \nnecessary and appropriate support to the DCSA in a timely manner to \nenable it to fulfill its responsibilities under this order; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 18:02 Apr 26, 2019 Jkt 247001 PO 00000 Frm 00006 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\29APE0.SGM 29APE0khammond on DSKBBV9HB2PROD with PRES DOC\n=== PDF page 5 of 7 ===\n18129 Federal Register / Vol. 84, No. 82 / Monday, April 29, 2019 / Presidential Documents \n(iv) no later than June 24, 2019, provide the Secretary of Defense with \na complete inventory of NBIB personnel, resources, and assets, and other \nOffice of Personnel Management personnel and resources that primarily \nsupport NBIB; \n(v) no later than June 24, 2019, execute a written agreement with the \nSecretary of Defense designating the appropriate support functions to be \ntransferred as part of the investigative mission, consistent with section \n925(d)(2)(B) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year \n2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note), as described in section 2.6(b)(viii) of this \norder; \n(vi) immediately upon the finalization of the agreement described in \nparagraph (v) of this subsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this order, \ncommence efforts to transition transferred or delegated functions and, \nas appropriate, associated Office of Personnel Management authorities, \noperations, resources, and personnel, to the DCSA; \n(vii) during the transition period, coordinate with the Department of \nDefense regarding any decisions concerning NBIB’s personnel structure, \nfinances, contracts, or organization to the extent provided in the written \nagreement described by paragraph (b)(viii) of this section; \n(viii) no later than September 30, 2019, complete the transfer of all \ndesignated administrative and operational functions to the Department \nof Defense and revoke any applicable delegation or designation to NBIB \nof investigative or other authority; and \n(ix) in the event the agreement described in paragraph (v) of this sub-\nsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this order is not executed by June 24, \n2019, beginning on such date, the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement shall begin to take necessary actions to begin execution of \nparagraphs (iii) through (viii) of this subsection until the agreement de-\nscribed in paragraph (v) of this subsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this \norder is executed, at which time the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement shall ensure actions subject to such agreement under para-\ngraphs (iii) through (viii) of this subsection are executed in accordance \nwith its terms.’’ \n‘‘(f) The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall: \n(i) facilitate an effective transfer of functions, including personnel and \nresources; \n(ii) support the Department of Defense’s efforts to establish a single, \ncentralized funding capability for its background investigations, as required \nby section 925(e)(1) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal \nYear 2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note); \n(iii) mediate any disagreements between the Secretary of Defense and \nthe Director of the Office of Personnel Management that may arise during \nor outside of the transition period and facilitate resolution of the conflicting \npositions; and \n(iv) develop, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and the \nDirector of the Office of Personnel Management, an appropriate funding \nplan for the activities undertaken pursuant to this order.’’ \n(f) Sections 2.4(b) and 2.5(e)(vi) of Executive Order 13467 are further \namended by striking ‘‘National Background Investigations Bureau’’ each place \nit appears and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Defense Counterintelligence and \nSecurity Agency.’’ \nSec. 3."},{"char_end":22367,"char_start":21727,"text":"Any reference to the Defense Secu-\nrity Service or NBIB in any Executive Order or other Presidential document \nthat is in effect on the day before the date of this order shall be deemed \nor construed to be a reference to the Defense Counterintelligence and Security \nAgency or any other entity that the Secretary of Defense names, consistent \nwith section 2(b)(i) of Executive Order 13467, and agencies whose regulations, \nrules, or other documents reference the Defense Security Service or NBIB \nshall revise any such respective regulations, rules, or other documents as \nsoon as practicable to update them for consistency with this order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13869","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted. Effective date depends on agency, publication or an unstated event.","provision_label":"Sec. 3.","reaches_target_via":"","savings_phrases":[],"scope":"partial","signing_date":"2019-04-24","target_id":"EO:12171","verb":"amend"}

1104(b) of title 5, United States Code; \n(iii) work in coordination with the Secretary of Defense to reassign \nappropriate resources, including personnel, to the DCSA and provide all \nnecessary and appropriate support to the DCSA in a timely manner to \nenable it to fulfill its responsibilities under this order; \nVerDate Sep<11>2014 18:02 Apr 26, 2019 Jkt 247001 PO 00000 Frm 00006 Fmt 4705 Sfmt 4790 E:\\FR\\FM\\29APE0.SGM 29APE0khammond on DSKBBV9HB2PROD with PRES DOC\n=== PDF page 5 of 7 ===\n18129 Federal Register / Vol. 84, No. 82 / Monday, April 29, 2019 / Presidential Documents \n(iv) no later than June 24, 2019, provide the Secretary of Defense with \na complete inventory of NBIB personnel, resources, and assets, and other \nOffice of Personnel Management personnel and resources that primarily \nsupport NBIB; \n(v) no later than June 24, 2019, execute a written agreement with the \nSecretary of Defense designating the appropriate support functions to be \ntransferred as part of the investigative mission, consistent with section \n925(d)(2)(B) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year \n2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note), as described in section 2.6(b)(viii) of this \norder; \n(vi) immediately upon the finalization of the agreement described in \nparagraph (v) of this subsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this order, \ncommence efforts to transition transferred or delegated functions and, \nas appropriate, associated Office of Personnel Management authorities, \noperations, resources, and personnel, to the DCSA; \n(vii) during the transition period, coordinate with the Department of \nDefense regarding any decisions concerning NBIB’s personnel structure, \nfinances, contracts, or organization to the extent provided in the written \nagreement described by paragraph (b)(viii) of this section; \n(viii) no later than September 30, 2019, complete the transfer of all \ndesignated administrative and operational functions to the Department \nof Defense and revoke any applicable delegation or designation to NBIB \nof investigative or other authority; and \n(ix) in the event the agreement described in paragraph (v) of this sub-\nsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this order is not executed by June 24, \n2019, beginning on such date, the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement shall begin to take necessary actions to begin execution of \nparagraphs (iii) through (viii) of this subsection until the agreement de-\nscribed in paragraph (v) of this subsection and section 2.6(b)(viii) of this \norder is executed, at which time the Director of the Office of Personnel \nManagement shall ensure actions subject to such agreement under para-\ngraphs (iii) through (viii) of this subsection are executed in accordance \nwith its terms.’’ \n‘‘(f) The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall: \n(i) facilitate an effective transfer of functions, including personnel and \nresources; \n(ii) support the Department of Defense’s efforts to establish a single, \ncentralized funding capability for its background investigations, as required \nby section 925(e)(1) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal \nYear 2018 (10 U.S.C. 1564 note); \n(iii) mediate any disagreements between the Secretary of Defense and \nthe Director of the Office of Personnel Management that may arise during \nor outside of the transition period and facilitate resolution of the conflicting \npositions; and \n(iv) develop, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense and the \nDirector of the Office of Personnel Management, an appropriate funding \nplan for the activities undertaken pursuant to this order.’’ \n(f) Sections 2.4(b) and 2.5(e)(vi) of Executive Order 13467 are further \namended by striking ‘‘National Background Investigations Bureau’’ each place \nit appears and inserting in lieu thereof ‘‘Defense Counterintelligence and \nSecurity Agency.’’ \nSec. 3."},{"char_end":21759,"char_start":21119,"text":"Any reference to the Defense Secu-\nrity Service or NBIB in any Executive Order or other Presidential document \nthat is in effect on the day before the date of this order shall be deemed \nor construed to be a reference to the Defense Counterintelligence and Security \nAgency or any other entity that the Secretary of Defense names, consistent \nwith section 2(b)(i) of Executive Order 13467, and agencies whose regulations, \nrules, or other documents reference the Defense Security Service or NBIB \nshall revise any such respective regulations, rules, or other documents as \nsoon as practicable to update them for consistency with this order."}],"exceptions_text":[],"filing_date":null,"id":"ACT:EO:12171>EO:13869@1e8037027e0b6f70","names_target":true,"notes":"Machine lead only; no legal ending or revival asserted.
